description: The green outline on the left encloses the unselected candidates. The small blue boxes on the right hold the selected elements. After the initial frame, each step shows the end of an entire round. Individual comparisons within a round are omitted.

steps.announcement: The initial array is [1, 7, 6, 3, 2], and the target is k = 3.
steps.explanation: Here k=3 and selection has not begun. The green box on the left holds [1, 7, 6, 3, 2]. The selected region on the right is empty. The prompt reads “Scan for the largest element.”
steps.key_state: The initial candidates are [1, 7, 6, 3, 2], k = 3, and the selected result is empty.
steps.title: Initialize the array and set k = 3

steps.announcement: The first scan selects the maximum, 7, leaving [1, 6, 3, 2] in the candidate region.
steps.explanation: In round one, select the maximum, 7, from the five candidates and move it to the blue box on the right. The left side holds [1, 6, 3, 2], the selected region holds [7], and the extraction order so far is [7]. The prompt reads “Round 1 finds the largest element.”
steps.key_state: After round one, the left side holds [1, 6, 3, 2], the selected region on the right holds [7], and the extraction order is [7].
steps.title: Select the maximum, 7

steps.announcement: The second scan selects the second largest value, 6, leaving [1, 3, 2] in the candidate region.
steps.explanation: In round two, select 6 from the remaining candidates and place it to the left of the selected 7. The left side holds [1, 3, 2], the right side reads [6, 7] from left to right, and the extraction order is [7, 6]. The prompt reads “Round 2 finds the second largest element.”
steps.key_state: After round two, the left side holds [1, 3, 2], the right side reads [6, 7] from left to right, and the extraction order is [7, 6].
steps.title: Select the remaining maximum, 6

steps.announcement: Round three selects 3. The result on the right is [3, 6, 7]. All three values have been selected, so the remaining [1, 2] on the left need no further comparisons.
steps.explanation: In round three, select 3 and place it at the far left of the selected region. The left side holds [1, 2], the right side reads [3, 6, 7] from left to right, and the extraction order is [7, 6, 3]. The prompt reads “Round 3 finds the third largest element.” All k=3 values have been selected, so comparisons stop.
steps.key_state: After round three, the left side holds [1, 2], the right side reads [3, 6, 7] from left to right, and the extraction order is [7, 6, 3]. Three values have been selected, so stop.
steps.title: Select the remaining maximum, 3

prose.summary: In each round, find the largest unselected element. Once selected, an element is excluded from later rounds.
prose.title: Selecting the top k by repeated scans

context: The example has five inputs and k=3. The four rows show, from top to bottom, the initial array and the states after three rounds of selection. Unselected values are on the left. The blue boxes on the right hold selected values.

Each newly selected element goes at the left end of the selected region on the right. The displayed left-to-right order is therefore the reverse of the extraction order. This placement involves no additional sorting.
description: Thick gray downward arrows mark successive rounds. Thin curved arrows mark the maximum extracted each round. The table's unselected and selected columns correspond to the left and right regions in the diagram. “Extraction order so far” lists the values chronologically and does not represent a separate array in the diagram.

frames.explanation: In each round, compare only the unselected elements on the left. The 6 selected in round two goes to the left of 7, and the 3 selected in round three goes to the left of 6. Selected values stay on the right.
frames.title: Selecting the top k by repeated scans

result: After k linear scans, all k largest elements have been found. The total time complexity is O(nk).
